name: Salesforce
summary: No Salesforce approval is needed to let customer orgs connect, but the ground moved in Spring '26: creating new Connected Apps is disabled by default in all orgs, so new integrations should use External Client Apps (ECAs). Multi-tenant distribution also means packaging the ECA and dealing with each customer's admin policies.
difficulty_reason: Self-serve, but ECAs are new, much older tutorials are now wrong, and customer org admins control who may use your app.

effort.hands_on: 1-3 h (ECA + test); more if you package it for distribution
effort.production: Days (packaging + customer admin approvals); AppExchange security review only if you list there
effort.waiting_on: Customer admins' policies (pre-authorisation, IP restrictions); optional AppExchange security review.

bottom_line: Use a free Developer Edition org as your 'home' org, create an External Client App with the authorization-code flow + PKCE and the narrowest scopes (api, refresh_token, often id/openid). Ignore tutorials that start with 'New Connected App' - since Spring '26 that path is off by default. Because customer org admins can restrict access, ship a short admin-setup page alongside your connect button.
app_type: External Client App (Setup > External Client App Manager) with OAuth settings enabled. Legacy Connected Apps keep working but new ones require a Salesforce Support exception.

scope_paths.name: Read/write CRM data via REST
scope_paths.review: None from Salesforce; customer admins may need to approve/pre-authorise

scope_paths.name: Full access
scope_paths.review: None, but security-conscious admins will push back

prerequisites.detail: Free; acts as the org that owns your app.
Plus decide whether to support sandbox orgs (test.salesforce.com) and My Domain logins.
Policies like 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized' block users until an admin acts.

stages.name: Create the External Client App
stages.goal: You have a consumer key/secret for an ECA with OAuth enabled.

steps.title: Sign up for a Developer Edition org
Create a new External Client App
steps.detail: Setup > Quick Find 'External Client App Manager' > New. Enable OAuth, add callback URL, select scopes (api, refresh_token, openid), require PKCE.

steps.title: Set policies and retrieve consumer key/secret
steps.detail: Configure refresh token policy (e.g. valid until revoked) and permitted users; copy credentials.

stages.name: Wire up and test
stages.goal: Your agent can call the REST API for a connected org.

steps.title: Implement web-server flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Authorise at https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize (or the user's My Domain / test.salesforce.com for sandboxes). Store instance_url from the token response and call that host.

steps.title: Test against a sandbox and a My Domain org
steps.detail: Many customers log in via My Domain; make the login host configurable.

stages.name: Distribute to customer orgs
stages.goal: Customer users can connect under their admins' policies.

steps.title: Package the ECA if you need it installed in subscriber orgs
steps.detail: Local ECAs are not copied into sandboxes or other orgs; packaged ECAs are.

steps.title: Publish an admin setup guide
steps.detail: Agent drafts steps for admins: approve the app, assign permission sets, relax IP restrictions if needed.

token_facts.value: Requires the refresh_token (offline_access) scope; lifetime set by app policy
Use instance_url returned per org - never hard-code

gotchas.title: New Connected Apps disabled (Spring '26)
gotchas.detail: Creation is off by default in all orgs via UI and API; a temporary Support exception exists but Salesforce says it will be removed. Use ECAs.

gotchas.title: ECAs don't support the username-password flow
gotchas.detail: Use authorization code (users) or JWT bearer / client credentials (server-to-server).

gotchas.title: Sandbox vs production login hosts
gotchas.detail: Sandbox users authenticate at test.salesforce.com; My Domain users at their own domain.

gotchas.title: Local ECAs aren't copied to sandboxes
gotchas.detail: Only packaged ECAs survive sandbox refresh/clone.

blockers.symptom: 'New Connected App' button missing or creation fails
blockers.next_step: Create an External Client App instead.

blockers.cause: Customer org policy requires admin pre-authorisation.
blockers.next_step: Send the admin setup guide; admin assigns the app via profile/permission set.

blockers.symptom: invalid_grant: authentication failure for sandbox users
blockers.next_step: Use test.salesforce.com or the org's My Domain.

agent_can: Pick the minimal scopes and policies
Write the PKCE web-server flow with configurable login hosts
Draft the customer admin setup guide
Translate old Connected App tutorials to ECA equivalents
Probe OIDC discovery for each customer's My Domain
you_must: Sign up for a Developer Edition org and create the ECA
Decide whether to pursue AppExchange (security review)

claims.claim: Spring '26 disables new Connected App creation by default in all orgs, via UI and API; existing Connected Apps keep working.
claims.note: Checked 2026-11-03 in a vendor's docs that quote Salesforce; Salesforce's own release-note page did not render for our fetcher (CSS error) and developer.salesforce.com returned 403. Search results summarising Salesforce's developer docs agree.

claims.claim: ECAs do not support the PASSWORD (username-password) flow.
Local ECAs are not copied on sandbox clone/refresh; packaged ECAs are.
login.salesforce.com OIDC discovery advertises PKCE S256 and authorization_code + refresh_token grants.
No Salesforce review is required for customer orgs to authorise an app; AppExchange security review applies only to listings.
claims.note: Standard behaviour, not re-checked against a specific Salesforce page in this pass.

open_questions: Confirm the ECA creation UI path and default policies directly in a Developer Edition org - not tested here.
A third-party guide mentions device-flow changes on 30 Nov 2026; not verified against Salesforce docs.
